entities.name: Abd al-Muttalib
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib (born Shayba ibn Hāshim, c. 497 – 579 CE) was a pivotal figure in pre-Islamic Mecca, serving as the fourth chief of the Quraysh tribal confederation and, most significantly, as the paternal grandfather and guardian of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. His life spanned a critical period of transition in the Hejaz, bridging the ancient tribal customs with the nascent stirrings that would lead to Islam. As the head of the Banu Hashim clan, he held immense political and religious authority, particularly due to his role as the custodian of the Kaaba and the sacred well of Zamzam, reinforcing his status as a central pillar of Meccan society.

His leadership was marked by several key events, including the rediscovery and restoration of the Zamzam well, which had been lost for centuries, thus re-establishing Mecca's vital water source and pilgrimage infrastructure. Perhaps the most famous event associated with him is the "Year of the Elephant" (Am al-Fil) in 570 CE, when he famously confronted Abraha al-Ashram, the Aksumite general, who attempted to destroy the Kaaba. According to tradition, Abd al-Muttalib declared, 'The House has a Lord who will defend it,' a prophecy fulfilled by the miraculous repulsion of Abraha's army, which cemented his spiritual authority and the sanctity of the Kaaba just prior to Muhammad's birth.

Abd al-Muttalib's primary legacy lies in his direct lineage to Muhammad and his crucial role in safeguarding the future prophet during his early childhood. Following the early deaths of his son Abd Allah (Muhammad's father) and daughter-in-law Amina, Abd al-Muttalib took Muhammad into his personal care, nurturing him for eight years until his own death. This period of guardianship ensured Muhammad's survival and upbringing within the most respected clan of Mecca, providing him with early exposure to the city's political and social dynamics, and establishing a foundational connection to the custodianship of the Kaaba.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Abd al-Muttalib's paramount historical significance stems from his direct guardianship of the future prophet Muhammad, ensuring his survival and early development within Mecca's most influential clan, and his role in upholding the sanctity of the Kaaba before Islam's advent.
